identity.name: Airfloa Rail Technology Limited
identity.industry: Rail Components & Interiors / Rolling-Stock Engineering (railway interiors, seating, integrated coach systems; emerging Defence & Aerospace)

summary.oneLiner: Recently-IPO'd Chennai rail-interiors maker (Vande Bharat / Amrit Bharat / metro seating, FRP & aluminium interiors, turnkey coach systems) printed FY26 revenue INR 319.6 cr (+66% YoY) and PAT INR 39.1 cr (+52%), but EBITDA margin compressed ~25%→20.1% as an >80% aluminium and >60% stainless-steel price spike outran its partial PVC cover. Management deliberately walked away from low-margin tenders — pushing the old INR 1,000 cr-revenue aspiration out modestly — and guides FY27 revenue ~INR 500 cr at 12–13% PAT margin on a INR 486.9 cr order book + INR 1,200 cr bid pipeline (~75% railways), funded by INR 120 cr fresh debt and a strong receivables collection rather than equity. Optionality sits in coach refurbishment (~INR 26,000 cr national programme), a Big Bang Boom defence JV (drones/EW), and a flexible-electronics subsidiary.

Management deliberately walked away from low-margin tenders — pushing the old INR 1,000 cr-revenue aspiration out modestly — and guides FY27 revenue ~INR 500 cr at 12–13% PAT margin on a INR 486.9 cr order book + INR 1,200 cr bid pipeline (~75% railways), funded by INR 120 cr fresh debt and a strong receivables collection rather than equity. financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | H2/FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (FY26) | INR 319.6 cr | +66% (vs INR 192.4 cr FY25) | H2-heavy (railway ordering/spend back-ended) |
| Revenue (H2 FY26) | INR 229.1 cr | +114% (vs INR 107.3 cr H2 FY25) | ~71% of full-year revenue in H2 |
| EBITDA / margin | INR 64.2 cr · 20.1% | +33% | Margin fell from ~25% on aluminium (+>80%) & SS (+60–65%) inflation; PVC covered only ~50–60% |
| PAT / margin | INR 39.1 cr · 12.2% | +52% | Held PAT margin despite RM hit via cost-cutting, price-blocking, supplier advances |
| Order book | INR 486.9 cr (unexecuted, as of May 2026) | — | ~INR 415–420 cr govt, ~INR 50–55 cr non-govt; ~INR 29 cr defence/aero in current book |
| Bid pipeline | ~INR 1,200 cr | — | ~INR 900 cr railways; ~INR 120 cr metro; ~INR 60–70 cr defence (HAL) |
| Return ratios | ROE 22.4% · ROCE ~24.9% | — | Strong; net debt/equity 0.2x |
| Receivables | INR 214 cr (31-Mar-26) | up (March-loaded sales) | ~20% collected by May-end; ~70% expected by Jun-end (~INR 100–110 cr inflow this month) |
> One-offs / distortions: other-expenses rose on higher CSR, bill-discounting charges, and FX procurement costs; finance cost fell despite scale (lower processing cost, repayments, fewer delayed-payment charges). R&D to be **capitalised on the balance sheet**, not expensed — so the planned 8–9%-of-sales R&D will NOT hit reported P&L margin.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue:** FY27 ~INR 500 cr (~+56% on INR 320 cr); ~75% covered by existing INR 486.9 cr book + ~30–40% of the INR 1,200 cr pipeline executing in-year. Two-shift run-rate alone gets to ~INR 400–450 cr; channel partners + new infra add the rest.
- **Margin:** FY27 PAT margin 12–13% (won't go below 12%); selective bidding to protect margin.
- **FY28+ ambition:** "if everything goes good," ~INR 1,000 cr revenue & ~INR 150 cr PAT — possibly even FY27, but the firm INR 1,000 cr milestone is pushed out "modestly" vs the earlier March-end aspiration.
- **Capex:** ~INR 30–35 cr in FY27 for a new 14-acre facility (50,000–1,00,000 sq ft initial shed, scaling to 3–4 lakh sq ft) — funded by term loan; intended to ~double capacity (currently ~90% utilised).
- **Funding:** INR 120 cr fresh debt @8.25% (INR 60 cr sanctioned, INR 60 cr by 15–30 Jun); **no equity in FY27** (FY28 equity possible once R&D matures).
- **Order intake:** targeting ~INR 100 cr of refurbishment orders this year; ~20–25% historical bid-win ratio; 20–25% inflow CAGR called "conservative."
- **Working capital:** target working-cycle ~60–70 days (from 90–95) and receivable days ~60–70 within 3–4 months.
order book & pipeline:
- Unexecuted order book INR 486.9 cr (May 2026); govt ~INR 415–420 cr / non-govt ~INR 50–55 cr; defence-aero ~INR 29 cr (executes FY27).
- Bid pipeline ~INR 1,200 cr: railways ~INR 900 cr (Atmanirbhar Bharat coach, "Spark" coach, Kavach coach, Vande Bharat sleeper), metro ~INR 120 cr (already holds ~INR 70 cr metro orders), defence ~INR 60–70 cr (predominantly HAL). Many first-time defence bids deliberately excluded from the INR 1,200 cr.
- 3-year focus contracts: Vande Bharat sleeper platform, Amrit Bharat turnkey, Kolkata Metro turnkey; plus Karnataka regional-transport (awarded to ICF), and coach **refurbishment** (~INR 26,000 cr sanctioned nationally; ~25,000 coaches over 3–4 yrs) — targeting ~INR 100 cr refurb orders this year.
- Customers: end-customer is Indian Railways / production units (ICF, MCF, RCF) and zonal railways; also supplies Tier-1s Siemens, Alstom, BEML on structured monthly schedules.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Rail interiors (core):** transitioning from component supplier to integrated engineering platform — complete interiors, assemblies, integrated coach systems, turnkey design-manufacture-supply-install-commission. Seating is a key line (competes with Tata–Fainsa JV, a Korean co, others).
- **Metro & high-speed:** metro a long-term growth leg (~INR 70 cr held + ~INR 120 cr pipeline); recently entered high-speed segment with a small contract.
- **Refurbishment:** large multi-year national programme; sets up regional **channel-partner** execution model (partner holds EMD/BG/PBG and local facility; Airfloa manufactures from Chennai, shares limited margin) — asset-light scaling lever.
- **Defence & Aerospace:** foundational year. AMCA-linked **simulators / G22 simulators** for HAL (prototypes approved, regular orders awaited — explicitly NOT AMCA airframe production). Big Bang Boom JV (incorporation by 15-Jun-26): autonomous drones (design near-complete) + electronic-warfare / high-power-microwave-laser systems; JV holds technology, Airfloa gets manufacturing rights; ~INR 25 cr commitment; revenue more likely FY27–28.
- **Flexible electronics (new subsidiary):** electroluminescent dynamic display boards / signage for railway network + aerospace/space; "deep technology," possible small revenue this year (not yet in order book).
- **Kavach-adjacent:** an AI-based remote-access "integrated security system" (distinct from RDSO Kavach 4.2) in mature internal stage; to be demoed to Railway Board / RDSO this year.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Coach refurbishment (~INR 26,000 cr / ~25,000 coaches) — the biggest near-term volume pool.
- Defence/EW JV (drones, EW, HPM-laser) — large but long-gestation (6–12 month trials post-prototype); could lift defence book to INR 150–200 cr "if certain programs happen faster."
- Flexible-electronics / EL display subsidiary — inorganic, short-gestation (railway customer), un-modelled upside.
- Channel-partner network — turns a INR 500 cr base into a INR 1,000–2,000 cr scalable platform without heavy capex.
margins & cost dynamics:
- RM is >60% of product cost; aluminium (ingots/extrusions/sheets/coils) is the dominant input (+>80% YoY); stainless steel +60–65%. PVC clauses cover only ~50–60% of RM moves; another ~30–35% of assembly cost (glass, rubbers, composites, fasteners, consumables) has **no** PVC. Net RM-shock absorbed restricted to ~20–25% (vs potential 80–90%) via vendor price-blocking, advances, LCs/BGs.
- Channel-partner / asset-light model claimed margin- and WC-accretive (no EMD/BG/PBG parking, lower infra & overhead; limited margin share).
- FX procurement costs and CSR raised other-expenses; finance cost fell despite higher scale.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- New 14-acre facility (land acquired): 50,000–1,00,000 sq ft initial shed → 3–4 lakh sq ft target; ~INR 30–35 cr FY27 (term-loan funded); consolidates 7 units to ~2, saving ~INR 20–25 lakh/month rent; aims to ~double capacity. Will not contribute much to FY27 topline (FY28 lever).
- **Machinery delay (watch):** high-precision machines (mostly China-sourced, IPO-funded) stalled by a new Chinese end-user-certificate requirement (Jan-2026); company may switch to advanced lightweight-interior machinery instead. Management insists this does NOT threaten the FY27 INR 500 cr target (two primary "missions"/machines already secured).
- Capacity currently ~90% utilised; two-shift system running since ~Dec-2025.
capital allocation:
- INR 120 cr fresh debt @8.25%; net debt/equity 0.2x; no FY27 equity raise (FY28 possible).
- R&D capitalised to balance sheet (8–9% of sales planned, mainly defence/aerospace), not expensed.
- Recently IPO'd; IPO proceeds partly earmarked for machinery (now delayed) and infra.
risks & watch-items:
- **Commodity inflation** (aluminium/SS) vs incomplete PVC cover — the key margin swing factor.
- **Working-capital strain / negative operating & free cash flow** — INR 214 cr receivables, March-loaded sales; collection target (70% by Jun-end) is the near-term proof point.
- **China machinery / end-user-certificate** risk to IPO-funded capex (mitigated, per mgmt).
- **Execution lumpiness** — railway ordering historically back-ends ~40% into Q4 (15–20 yr trend); de-skewing only partial.
- **Guidance credibility** — INR 1,000 cr milestone already pushed out once; FY28 INR 1,000 cr / INR 150 cr PAT is aspirational and capacity/R&D-dependent.
- **R&D capitalisation** — flatters reported margin; watch for future impairments if defence/EW programs stall (long 6–12 month trial cycles).
- **Channel-partner model** — execution/quality control across third parties is unproven at scale.
- **Customer concentration** — Indian Railways / production units dominate; govt is ~85% of book.
management quality / tone: - MD candid and detailed; openly explained the margin compression, the deliberate walk-away from low-margin tenders, and the deferred INR 1,000 cr target. Promotional on long-dated optionality (defence JV "big surprise," flexible-electronics "deep technology," FY28 INR 1,000 cr "even this year") and somewhat repetitive/qualitative on numbers. Strong on advisor pedigree (Sudhanshu Mani, Tilak Seth). R&D-capitalisation answer was firm but is a quality flag to monitor.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Reported 12.2% PAT margin is real, but R&D (8–9% of sales) being capitalised rather than expensed means underlying earnings quality is softer than the headline — a key thing to verify next quarter.
- The structural pivot is from product-supplier to **turnkey integrator + asset-light channel-partner network**, explicitly to scale to INR 1,000–2,000 cr without proportional capex — the model, not the order book, is the story.
- Refurbishment (~INR 26,000 cr national pool) is the most credible near-term growth driver; defence/EW is genuine optionality but 2–3 years out with binary trial risk.
- It is a **rail-capex picks-and-shovels** name (interiors/seating into Vande Bharat, Amrit Bharat, metro, HSR) — a Tier-2/3 supplier to ICF/MCF/RCF and to Siemens/Alstom/BEML, leveraged to India's coach-build and refurbishment cycle.
- "AIRFLOA" is a BSE-only scrip; no NSE listing — liquidity/identity caveat for screening.

hero.oneLiner: Recently-IPO'd Chennai rail-interiors maker (Vande Bharat / Amrit Bharat / metro seating, FRP & aluminium interiors, turnkey coach systems) printed FY26 revenue INR 319.6 cr (+66% YoY) and PAT INR 39.1 cr (+52%), but EBITDA margin compressed ~25%→20.1% as an >80% aluminium and >60% stainless-steel price spike outran its partial PVC cover. Management deliberately walked away from low-margin tenders — pushing the old INR 1,000 cr-revenue aspiration out modestly — and guides FY27 revenue ~INR 500 cr at 12–13% PAT margin on a INR 486.9 cr order book + INR 1,200 cr bid pipeline (~75% railways), funded by INR 120 cr fresh debt and a strong receivables collection rather than equity. Optionality sits in coach refurbishment (~INR 26,000 cr national programme), a Big Bang Boom defence JV (drones/EW), and a flexible-electronics subsidiary.
